title: Introduce circuit quiesce mode and humane load-shedding policy
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a cluster-level quiesce mode and a tenant-aware 'humane' load-shedding policy. Feature flag default disabled. Rolling enable recommended for canary. No schema migrations.
description:
Motivation: We observed two recent incidents where aggressive immediate evictions during overload caused noisy failovers and cascading KV cache misses. This PR introduces a cluster-level 'quiesce' state and a gentle, tenant-aware load-shedding policy ("humane" shedding) designed to preserve in-flight work, minimize cold cache churn, and provide observable, reversible controls for SRE during incidents.

Design summary: The change has three coordinated pieces: 1) a new quiesce state for serving nodes which accepts in-flight requests but rejects or deprioritizes new low-priority admissions; 2) a lightweight admission controller that evaluates per-request priority, tenant SLO budget, and recent KV cache hit rate to make graded accept/reject decisions; 3) a soft-retry response surface (429 + Retry-After + origin TTL hint) and a console toggle with rollout controls. The admission decisions expose metrics and traces so ops can tune policies without a code rollback.

Key goals: preserve user-facing latency for high-priority requests, avoid mass reboots/evacuations, reduce downstream cache hammering during scale-down, and provide clear signals for progressive rollback.

What changed (high level): updated runtime/router: add QuiesceManager and humane-shed policy hook; admission controller: new EvaluateAdmission(request) path; config: feature flag 'serve.quiesce.enabled' and per-tenant soft-shed weights; telemetry: shed_decision{result,reason,tenant}, quiesce_state{node,ttl}, tenant_shed_rate.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for admission logic and priority buckets - [x] Integration test: quiesce acceptance behavior with in-flight requests - [x] Canary rollout plan documented in PR - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts stubbed - [x] Rollback and toggle via console/flag.

Operator notes: Enabling quiesce does not force node restarts. Nodes will enter quiesce for a configurable window (default 90s) where they allow existing streams to finish and triage new admissions. "Humane" shedding uses a sliding acceptance curve: low-priority requests are gradually given 429s with increasing Retry-After and suggested degrade hints. This is intentionally rate-limited and tenant-weighted to avoid punishing small tenants during fleet-wide stress.

Config snippet (pseudo): serve:   quiesce:     enabled: false     window_seconds: 90   humane_shed:     policy: tenant_weighted     base_rate: 0.03     escalation_step: 0.02

Canary plan: enable flag on a single canary region with verbose telemetry for 4 hours, monitor shed_decision, kv_miss_rate, p50/p95 latency for priority buckets; if any large tenant shows >5% error uplifts, auto-disable and escalate.

Related work: this PR complements ENG-1720 (kv-preserve flow) and SRE-77's incident playbook changes.

Rollback: feature flag off disables new paths and drains quiesce state; all admissions fallback to previous admission controller. No DB changes, so rollback is immediate.

Telemetry: emit shed_decision and quiesce_state metrics
Add unit/integration tests and canary runbook
review_thread: Evan Morales: Can we avoid a hard dependency on KV latency in EvaluateAdmission? Suggest fallbacks when KV is missing.
Priya Shah: Reply: admission treats missing KV telemetry as 'unknown' and falls back to tenant-weighting (see humane_shed.go: evaluateWithFallback()).
Sofia Li: Please add a unit test to cover the Retry-After header formatting for non-HTTP callers.
Priya Shah: Added test and updated integration run output (see commits).
Marcus Nguyen: Approving after minor nits addressed. Leaving small comment about metric cardinality.
testing: Local unit tests covering admission thresholds and priority bucketing
Integration test that spins a single node, marks it quiesce, asserts in-flight streams finish while new low-priority requests receive 429
Canary in us-west-2 for 4 hours with synthetic load and per-tenant telemetry
rollback_plan: Turn off serve.quiesce.enabled feature flag via console (immediate). If reverted rolling disable fails, revert the single squash commit that wires feature flag and restart canary nodes. No datastore migration required.
notes_from_ops: Observed during canary: quiesce_state metric reported expected transitions; tenant_shed_rate provided early signal to rollback for one medium tenant (manual rollback executed per plan). Overall latency for high-priority traffic improved by 6% during simulated surge.

Add runbook section for 'humane shedding' to incident playbook
Monitor metric cardinality and consider sampling for high-cardinality tenants
